The Blachernae Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Blachernae Icon of the Theotokos

Vlahernskaya · Blachernae Hodegetria

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The named Blachernae icon is a Hodegetria tradition connected with Constantinople and its later reception in Russia. It must be distinguished from the broad use of Blachernitissa for other Marian compositions.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 4, 5, 6

What is depicted

This illustration is a 1705 Blachernae example from the Spaso-Vlakhernsky monastery near Dmitrov, now in the St. Andrei Rublev Museum. The photograph is credited to user:bgds under CC BY-SA 3.0. It is an identified later example, not a claimed seventh-century original.

[2] Exact artwork file: Description, Creator, Date, Credit and licence fields; complete downloaded image visually compared

History and tradition

The OCA recounts an earlier transfer from Jerusalem to Constantinople and associates the icon with the city’s deliverance during siege. It later follows the image through Athos to Moscow, giving 1654 for its gift to Tsar Aleksei Mikhailovich. These are the source’s traditional historical claims.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3, 4, 5

The earlier Constantinopolitan episode names the empresses Eudokia and Pulcheria and the church where the revered robe of the Mother of God was preserved.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 3

Published explanation

The same page calls the icon Hodegetria, She Who Leads the Way, and connects its memory with praise of the Mother of God. Its heading prints July 7; the narrative also names July 2 and the Saturday of the Akathist. The movable observance is not reduced to a fixed civil date.

[1] Published account, paragraphs 4, 6
